Cortico-subcortico-muscular dynamics during reach-to-grasp in Parkinson's disease

Simultaneous scalp-EEG (126 ch) + STN-LFP (DBS lead) + EMG + kinematics, 8 patients OFF medication, self-paced reach-to-grasp. Full corrected analysis: spectral · connectivity · brain–behavior · brain–clinic. Data F:\Projects\Parkinson_ReachGrasp\Reprocessing; scripts in spectral_statistical_analysis/ and additional_analyses/.

One-paragraph summary. Across the reach-to-grasp sequence, STN and sensorimotor cortex show a robust, cross-modal post-movement beta rebound (PMBR) and a phase-structured β reorganization (reach desynchronizes, grip re-synchronizes). The STN couples to the contralateral sensorimotor cortex in β during grip (volume-conduction-free), a lateralized cortico-subcortical loop. Most importantly, single-trial STN β-ERD depth predicts movement speed (deeper ERD → faster reach) consistently across patients — establishing the spectral dynamics as behaviorally meaningful. Cortico-muscular routing and all clinical correlations are underpowered at n=8 and reported as exploratory.

LFP β-specific analyses7wue05 excluded on a pre-specifiable signal-quality rule: no detectable resting STN β peak (prominence 1.2 dB / SNR 1.3, vs 3–13 dB / 2.3–5.5 for all others). You cannot measure a β-ERD of a rhythm that isn't there.

Both exclusions are reported transparently and on principled grounds (task availability; signal quality), never on their effect on a result. Full-sample (n=8) numbers are given alongside the n=7 numbers wherever the β-peak rule is used.

Moving hand / laterality (ground truth: A02_events_segmentation.m ll. 91–96): wue05 & wue09 moved the left hand (contralateral cortex = right hemisphere); all others the right hand. A prior bug that conflated this with the EMG-dominant-set list had inverted contra/ipsi for 5/8 subjects in the connectivity code; now fixed, and all EEG analyses mirror-flip the two left-hand movers so "contralateral cortex" = left for every subject.

2 · Statistical framework (the central correction)

What the original pipeline did wrong. It pooled ~239 trials across subjects and tested them as independent observations (pseudoreplication), yielding p = 0.0001 — a value below the n=8 permutation floor (0.004), i.e. mathematically impossible under a correct null.

Every result here instead uses the subject as the unit of inference:

  • Exhaustive subject-level sign-flip permutation (2⁸ = 256; two-tailed floor 0.0078, one-tailed 0.0039). Cluster mass corrected over frequency / channel where applicable.
  • Trial information sharpens, never multiplies. Precision-weighted (DerSimonian–Laird) and one-way mixed-model variants of the cluster statistic were built and agreed with the subject-mean test — confirming n=8 is the binding constraint, not the trial count. (statsmodels REML was numerically unstable for the intercept-only LMM at the τ²=0 boundary; a closed-form ANOVA estimator was used instead.)
  • No double-dipping — the cluster/band p-value is the corrected inference; no post-hoc re-testing of selected bands.
  • Pre-specified families for canonical-band tests (FDR/Bonferroni), because at n=8 the permutation floor makes broadband FDR across 35–42 tests unsatisfiable for any effect size — pre-specification is required, not optional.
  • Coherences variance-stabilized with atanh√ before group tests; condition contrasts used throughout to cancel coherence's DOF-dependent positive bias and baseline nuisance.

3.2 Movement-related theta modulation

Pre-specified, two-tailed (direction not firmly established in STN): −0.55 dB, p = 0.008 (Bonferroni 0.023). Sign is baseline-dependent — it is a decrease relative to the immediate pre-movement window but an increase relative to a true (block-start) rest, reflecting a peri-movement low-frequency change. Interpret cautiously (possible movement-related low-frequency contamination; an EMG-regression control is advisable before claiming a neural θ effect).

3.3 The movement beta-ERD — a cautionary, fully-worked case

The movement β-ERD initially "vanished," then resolved once three real problems were fixed:

  1. Phase-lumping. The ballistic reach desynchronizes β; the sustained grasp/pull re-synchronize it. Averaging all "movement" phases cancels the ERD against the ERS.
  2. Baseline contamination. The −0.5→0 s baseline sits inside the desynchronization (β falls ~1 dB across that window), normalising the ERD away. A block-start rest baseline, and the baseline-free reach-vs-grip contrast, fix it.
  3. wue05 has no STN β peak → cannot show a β-ERD (handled by the signal-quality rule).
ContrastnResult
Reach − grip (baseline-free, whole β)8−0.70 dB, p = 0.039 (7/8) — most defensible single number
Reach high-β vs rest (β-peak group)7−1.29 dB, p = 0.016 (7/7)
Reach high-β vs rest (full sample)8−0.99 dB, p = 0.086 (trend)
Whole-spectrum movement ERD vs rest (freq-CBPT)8no cluster (broadband search dilutes a focused effect)
The β-ERD is real but modest: significant as a focused, pre-specified, baseline-free contrast; a trend at the full sample. Its functional reality is independently established by the single-trial behavioral coupling (§6) — which is the stronger evidence that this β modulation matters.

5 · Connectivity — cortico-subcortico-muscular

Per-subject multitaper CSD → coherence + partial coherence + (exploratory) Granger; subject-level inference on contrasts. Imaginary coherency used for all EEG-involving pairs (zero-lag/volume-conduction control).

5.1 STN ↔ cortex β coupling — the network result

FindingMagnitude cohImaginary coh (VC-free)Verdict
Grip: contra > ipsi STN-cortex βt=3.76, p=0.008t=4.65, p=0.008robust
Reach < grip (contra)t=−3.10, p=0.016t=−1.75, p=0.12suggestive
Rest / reach contra vs ipsip=0.09 / 0.65n.s.n.s.
During the sustained grip, STN β couples preferentially to the cortex contralateral to the moving hand — robust and volume-conduction-free. The pathological STN–M1 β loop is lateralized to the moving-limb hemisphere and expressed in the hold phase. Absolute STN–scalp coherence is low (~0.02–0.03, expected for deep↔scalp); the signal is the within-subject contra/ipsi contrast, confirmed by imaginary coherency.

5.2 Cortico-muscular coupling & routing — underpowered (honest null)

The cortico-muscular triad is underpowered at n=8 (scalp CMC is intrinsically weak). The routing question — is cortico-muscular coherence relayed through STN — is tested but not resolved: 7/8 patients show the predicted direction, but the effect is not significant. Report as a supplementary null, never a positive claim.

6 · Brain–behavior — single-trial β predicts movement speed

Within-subject trial-level (powered): per-subject Spearman ρ between trial neural state and trial behavior, aggregated to a group second-level sign-flip on Fisher-z. 217 trials, ~27/subject.

Neural (reach phase)Behaviormean ρgroup pconsistency
β-ERDreach duration+0.140.023 (FDR 0.046)7/8
β-ERDpeak velocity (m/s)−0.130.24 (trend)5/8 — same direction
β-ERDnormalized jerk · smoothness · amplitude≈0n.s.null (not a quality effect)
β-ERDsubmovement count——too discrete to test (most trials = 1)
The keystone result. Trial-by-trial, deeper STN β-ERD during reach predicts a faster (shorter-duration) reach, consistent across 7/8 patients (group p = 0.023; FDR q = 0.046 across the two pre-specified vigor metrics). With the full validated kinematics the coupling is specific to movement timing: peak velocity is directionally consistent (deeper ERD → faster, 5/8 trend) but smoothness (normalized jerk, smoothness index), amplitude and submovement decomposition are all null — an STN-β vigor/speed effect, not a movement-quality one. This single-trial coupling is what gives the modest group-mean β-ERD its functional meaning: 8 patients showed no significant ERD vs rest, yet ~27 trials/subject reveal a robust, reproducible brain–behavior relationship.

Caveats: within-subject effect sizes are modest (ρ≈0.14) but consistent and significant; duration is the robust readout (replicated across auto-derived and validated kinematics), peak velocity a directional trend. The validated metrics (kinematic_metrics.csv, 22 features) refine the result to movement timing specifically. Merged per-trial table: brain_behavior_merged.csv.

On machine-learning prediction of clinical scores from neural data: do not, at n=8. Clinical scores are one per patient → the inferential unit is the patient → n=8 is a hard ceiling no trial-level trick removes. With 8 samples you cannot train+validate; multi-feature models overfit (features ≫ samples) and report illusory accuracy. The evidence is above: even single-feature pre-specified correlations find nothing — ML, being more flexible and less powered per parameter, can only manufacture false fits. Legitimate ML here would be within-subject trial-level decoding of movement/state (not clinical), or clinical prediction with ~30+ patients.

8 · Limitations & recommended paper framing

Honest limitations

  • n = 8 is the binding constraint (normal for invasive human work, but it caps whole-scalp/whole-spectrum correction and all between-subject clinical inference). Pre-specified ROIs/bands and within-subject designs are where power lives.
  • The β-ERD is modest and partly baseline-dependent; report the baseline-free contrast and the single-trial coupling as the primary evidence.
  • Connectivity: STN↔cortex is robust; cortico-muscular routing is an honest null.
  • θ effect may carry movement-related low-frequency contamination — needs an EMG-regression control.
  • Two principled exclusions (wue04 no task; wue05 no β peak) — both pre-declared, full-sample numbers reported alongside.

Recommended narrative (one integrated paper — do not salami-slice)

"Phase-specific reorganization of the cortico-subthalamic beta network during reach-to-grasp in Parkinson's disease, and its single-trial behavioral relevance."

  1. Spectral backbone — cross-modal PMBR (STN p=0.008, EEG p=0.023) and phase-structured β (reach desync / grip resync).
  2. Network — lateralized STN↔contralateral-cortex β coupling during grip (VC-free, p=0.008).
  3. Behavioral relevance (keystone) — single-trial β-ERD depth predicts movement speed (group p≈0.02–0.03).
  4. Supporting/exploratory — cortico-muscular routing (null) and clinical associations (hypothesis-generating), clearly flagged.

The novelty is the integration (multimodal + kinematic-phase + single-trial behavior), not any single known effect. Target: a strong specialty journal (J Neurophysiol, Clinical Neurophysiology, Neurobiol Dis, Brain Stimulation, NeuroImage:Clinical, eNeuro). The rigorous, honest small-n statistics are a selling point, not a liability.
